A running OpenFarm installation. Start with Docker installation if you do not have one. An account with permission to add printers, manage filament and parts, and create print jobs. The first administrator can complete this walkthrough. A supported printer reachable from the OpenFarm server. A small, known-good sliced 3MF made for that printer and nozzle, plus the matching physical filament.

Open your installation's address, normally http://<server-ip>:6868. Use the administrator username and password configured at first startup. If no password was configured, the initial defaults are admin / admin-openfarm. Change that password in My profile → Security. There is no public sign-up flow; an administrator creates additional accounts in Users & groups.

Go to Printers → Add printer. Select a discovered printer or enter its connection details manually. Choose a name and supply the credential requested for the model. Adding the printer checks the connection before saving it. For model-specific preparation, follow Bambu Lab or Snapmaker U1. Wait for the printer to become reachable and report its nozzle size. Open the printer's Edit page. Select a compatible machine profile, process profile, and build plate, then save. Profile options come from the installed slicer catalog.

Open Filament → Add filament and create the material, vendor, and color you will use. Configure that filament's profile assignment for your printer model and nozzle. A color can inherit the filament's assignment or override it. Use Add spools to register the physical spool and its remaining weight. Physically load the spool, then use Load spool to associate it with the correct printer feed slot. A printer-reported material does not replace a tracked spool. OpenFarm needs both the physical configuration and its inventory record. See Filament catalog and Spools.

Go to Parts → Add part. Upload the file. Wait for background processing to finish. Review the file information. For a multi-plate upload, review the plates you want to save. Select the Production filament that matches the loaded spool's catalog color. Complete any missing print requirements. Save the part. Ready to print means its requirements are complete. OpenFarm checks printer compatibility separately. A missing estimate stays unknown. See Parts and files.

Open the part and choose Print. Request one plate, review the plan, and choose Send to queue. A production run is optional for this first print. Open Queue to follow the job. If it cannot start, open its status link or Job diagnosis on the job page. Printer matching explains each requirement and where to fix it.

documents.t: Check that the physical bed is empty, the correct plate is installed, and the printer is safe to start. If the printer is awaiting clearance, use Mark ready. A connected, idle printer with compatible loaded material can take queued work automatically. Automatic dispatch Sending work to the queue can start a compatible ready printer. Finish the physical checks before queueing work or marking a printer ready.
documents.s: 6. Clear the bed and mark ready

documents.t: Monitor the job from Queue, the printer page, or Dashboard. After printing, inspect the output, remove it from the bed, and mark the printer ready for the next job. If output needs confirmation or replacement, follow Outcomes and recovery.

Production runs track an order or batch with fixed quantities. Assemblies define products with multiple printed components. Maintenance tracks service intervals. Troubleshooting helps with connection and dispatch problems.
Administrators create accounts under Users & groups. There is no public self-registration or email password-recovery flow.

Choose Add user. Enter the username, email, and temporary password. Passwords require at least eight characters. Select the user's groups. Save the account. Ask the user to change the temporary password under My profile → Security.

Each user receives all permissions granted by their groups, plus permissions granted directly to that user. The permission editor offers None, View, Edit, Full, Custom for each area. Select sensitive permissions, such as remote printer control, explicitly. Administrators is protected and has every permission. Operators grants permissions for daily work, with limits on removal, administration, credentials, and remote control. Viewers grants read access to business information. The API enforces permissions even when a button or navigation link is hidden. A disabled control can mean the account can view an area but cannot change it. Keep at least one administrator account enabled. Before removing an ordinary group, remove its members.

Users connect AI assistants themselves, from My profile → Connected apps or with an access token: see AI assistants. Administrators can see and revoke a user's connected apps and tokens from that account's page.

My profile → Sessions lists active browser sessions and can sign out one or all devices. Administrators can revoke another user's sessions from that account's page. Browser sessions expire fourteen days after sign-in. Refreshing an access token does not extend this period. If you change your own password, your current browser session stays active and other sessions end. If an administrator resets the password, all sessions end. Either type of password change revokes personal access tokens. Disabling an account blocks and revokes its sessions and tokens. Enabling it again does not restore old credentials. See API access for personal tokens.

Another administrator can reset the password in Users & groups. The initial password settings apply only when OpenFarm creates the first account. They do not replace an existing password. Keep more than one trusted administrator account and test your installation backup.

OpenFarm runs an MCP server at /mcp on your installation. An AI assistant connected to it can read your farm (printers, the queue, production runs, parts, assemblies, filament stock, fee profiles, maintenance and farm stats) and make the changes you allow. It acts as you, with only the access you give it. There are two ways to connect: Way How For Sign in The assistant opens OpenFarm, you sign in and choose what it may do. Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code. Needs sign-in turned on. Access token You create a token and paste it into the assistant's settings. Any MCP client that can send a header, including on a LAN-only installation.

MCP is disabled by default. An administrator must enable it before any assistant can connect. Open Settings → AI assistants. Select Access tokens only for a compatible local client. For browser sign-in, first set the Public URL under Settings → Server, then select Sign-in and access tokens. Select Save. Changes apply without restarting OpenFarm. Connect from your assistant. Follow the sign-in or access-token steps below. Sign-in requires an HTTPS public URL. HTTP is allowed only for localhost development. Setting the public URL does not configure DNS, HTTPS, a tunnel, or a reverse proxy. For remote access, route the whole hostname to OpenFarm, including /mcp, /oauth/ and /.well-known/. Do not put another login wall in front of discovery or /oauth/token. See Configuration. Deployment settings can lock these controls. The page names the setting that controls the field. See deployment overrides. To check an enabled server, run: curl -i -X POST https://farm.example.com/mcp \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' Without a credential, the server returns 401. With sign-in enabled, its WWW-Authenticate header includes resource_metadata. A disabled server returns 404. Claude and ChatGPT on the web connect from the internet: the address must be reachable from there. An installation reachable only on your LAN can use Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code with an access token instead.

Use your installation address with /mcp at the end. For example, if the public URL is https://farm.example.com, use https://farm.example.com/mcp. Replace the example URL in each setup below. Assistant Setup Claude Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. Name: OpenFarm. URL: https://farm.example.com/mcp. ChatGPT Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings → turn on Developer mode, then create a connector with the URL and OAuth authentication. Claude Code claude mcp add --transport http openfarm https://farm.example.com/mcp, then run /mcp in Claude Code and choose Authenticate. Cursor Add {"mcpServers":{"openfarm":{"url":"https://farm.example.com/mcp"}}} to ~/.cursor/mcp.json. VS Code Add {"servers":{"openfarm":{"type":"http","url":"https://farm.example.com/mcp"}}} to .vscode/mcp.json. When the assistant connects, OpenFarm opens a Connect page, titled with the app's name, in your browser: Sign in to OpenFarm if asked. Check the account shown under the title. Check Returns to: it names the website or the app on your computer that receives the answer. The app name is supplied by the app itself and is not verified. Choose what the app may do. Reading is selected for you; changes and printer control never are. Choose Allow selected access. If you did not start this from your assistant just now, choose Cancel. A connection lasts 30 days. Then connect again from the assistant.

Open My profile → Access tokens → Add token. Name the token after the assistant, for example Claude Code. Select the read permissions the assistant needs, for example Printers: View and Queue: View. Create the token and copy the credential. OpenFarm shows it only once. Configure your assistant with the server URL and token. Use an example below. Use your installation address with /mcp at the end. Replace https://farm.example.com/mcp in the examples. A local client can use a LAN address, such as http://openfarm.local:6868/mcp. Store the credential securely. You can use a local environment variable such as OPENFARM_TOKEN to keep it out of a shared configuration file. This is a client credential, separate from the server settings.
claude mcp add --transport http openfarm https://farm.example.com/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $OPENFARM_TOKEN"

Set OPENFARM_TOKEN in the environment used to start Cursor. Add this configuration to ~/.cursor/mcp.json: { "mcpServers": { "openfarm": { "url": "https://farm.example.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:OPENFARM_TOKEN}" } } } }

Add this configuration to .vscode/mcp.json. VS Code asks for the token and stores it securely. { "inputs": [ { "type": "promptString", "id": "openfarm-token", "description": "OpenFarm access token", "password": true } ], "servers": { "openfarm": { "type": "http", "url": "https://farm.example.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:openfarm-token}" } } } }

Set OPENFARM_TOKEN in the environment used to start Codex. Add this configuration to ~/.codex/config.toml: [mcp_servers.openfarm] url = "https://farm.example.com/mcp" bearer_token_env_var = "OPENFARM_TOKEN"

Other clients need these settings: Setting Value Transport Streamable HTTP Server URL https://farm.example.com/mcp Header Authorization: Bearer <token> The assistant sees only the tools that both its access and your account allow. If you lose a permission, the assistant loses it on its next request.

"What needs my attention?" — printers awaiting clear, offline or alerting, jobs that cannot be sent and why, failed jobs, late runs, low filament and maintenance due. "Queue 20 keychains and 5 desk sets." or "Make a production run for Friday's market." — the assistant shows the plan (plates, print hours, filament, shortages) and queues it only after you agree. "I cleared the plates on P1 and P3." — marks those printers ready. "Why is the bracket job not printing?" — the checks each printer fails: nozzle, material, colour, plate or pin. "What filament should I order for the next six weeks?" — stock, use over the last 30 days, queued work and spools to buy per colour. "I received 10 spools of PLA Basic Black, 1 kg, 22 each." — adds them to stock. "Put the gridfinity parts in Storage/Gridfinity and tag them." — folders, names, tags and assemblies. "Add a Shopee fee profile: 18% commission and 0.50 per order." and "What does the desk set sell for on Shopee?" "Lubricate the rods every 200 print hours on all X1C printers."

With the matching access, an assistant can also: Change Sign-in choice Token permission Reorder, pin and unpin queued jobs Reorder, pin and requeue jobs Print jobs: Reorder, Pin Requeue a failed or cancelled job same Print jobs: Requeue Queue parts and assemblies, alone or as a production run Plan and queue parts and assemblies Production runs: Add Organize library folders, rename and tag parts, add and change assemblies Organize folders, rename and tag parts, and add or change assemblies Library: Organize; Parts: Change; Assemblies: Add, Change Add new spools to stock Add new spools to stock Spools: Add Add and change fee profiles Add and change fee profiles Settings: Change fees Add maintenance tasks, assign them to printers, mark them done Add and assign maintenance tasks, and mark maintenance done Maintenance: Change, Mark done Mark printers ready Mark printers ready after their plates are cleared Printers: Mark ready Pause a running print Pause running prints Print jobs: Remote control Cancel a job or stop a running print Cancel jobs and stop running prints Print jobs: Cancel Queueing, requeueing, marking ready, pausing and cancelling act on real printers: an idle printer can start the work at once, and a stopped print cannot be resumed. Queueing: the assistant first shows you the plan and queues exactly that plan only after you agree. Asking twice never queues it twice. Mark ready: the assistant marks a printer ready only when you tell it that printer's plate is clear. If another print ended on that printer after the assistant looked, it refuses and asks you again. Requeue, pause and cancel: the assistant shows you the job, the printer and its progress and waits for your confirmation. Cancel also checks that the job is still where the assistant saw it. Most assistants also ask you to approve each change. Allow printer control only for an assistant you watch. An assistant can never remove anything, resume prints, skip objects, or change settings other than fee profiles, printer connections, users or credentials. Each change appears in the activity log under your name, with the app or token name.

The assistant sends what it reads to its AI service. Give it only the access it needs. Names and notes in OpenFarm are shown to the assistant as data; it is told never to follow instructions found in them.

An administrator can select Disabled under Settings → AI assistants to block all MCP access. Changing the MCP mode or public URL disconnects signed-in apps and cancels pending connection requests. Re-enabling MCP does not restore those app connections. Personal access tokens keep their REST permissions and can use MCP again when token access is enabled. Work already accepted by a printer is not undone. A signed-in app: My profile → Connected apps → Revoke access. An administrator can do the same on the user's page. A token: My profile → Access tokens → Revoke. Changing your password, an administrator's password reset or disabling the account ends every connected app and token. An administrator's Revoke all on a user's sessions also ends their apps. Sign out and your own Revoke all sessions do not disconnect apps or tokens.

A signed-in connection lasts 30 days from when you allowed it. Lists return at most 100 items a page. The assistant does not get live updates; it reads again when you ask. Sign-in needs HTTPS (HTTP only for localhost).

401 Unauthorized: the token or sign-in is wrong, expired or revoked, or you sent a browser session instead. With sign-in on, the WWW-Authenticate header names resource_metadata, which the assistant uses to sign in. The assistant asks for an OAuth login, or says the server needs authentication it cannot do: sign-in is off. Prepare the server, or use an access token. MCP is disabled: ask an administrator to enable it under Settings → AI assistants. Sign-in is off: use an access token, or ask an administrator to set an HTTPS public URL and select Sign-in and access tokens. Connection request expired: the Connect page was open for more than 10 minutes, or was already used. Start again from the assistant. Discovery returns HTML: your proxy sends /.well-known/ or /oauth/ to another site or to a cached app page. Route the whole hostname to OpenFarm. 403 Forbidden (MCP origin check failed): a browser page called /mcp from another site. Use the assistant's own connector, desktop app or CLI. 405 on GET /mcp: normal. MCP uses POST only. A tool is missing: the assistant's access or your account lacks its permission. Connect again and allow it, or add the permission to a new token. Use the POST check in Prepare the server. A plain GET request returns 405 when MCP is enabled.
Open Settings from the user menu. Your permissions determine which sections you can open and whether you can save changes.

Set the farm currency, electricity rate, and failure allowance for estimates. The currency setting labels the farm's monetary values. It does not convert amounts between currencies. If you change the currency, review the prices already entered. Failure allowance ranges from zero to below 100% and defaults to zero. It increases estimated filament, depreciation, and electricity costs to allow for failed prints. It does not increase every product cost.

Administrators set the Public URL of the installation here. Leave it blank for local access. Sign-in for AI assistants needs an HTTPS URL, except for localhost development. With HTTPS configured, sign in through that address because refresh cookies become secure. The change applies without restarting and disconnects signed-in AI assistants. A deployment ORIGIN override makes this field read-only.

Administrators choose Disabled, Access tokens only, or Sign-in and access tokens. MCP is disabled by default. Changes take effect without restarting. See AI assistants for client setup and connection permissions.

Configure the purchase cost, depreciation settings, and average power for each printer model. OpenFarm combines these values with estimated print time and the electricity rate. The assembly's Build panel shows the resulting costs. Unknown values remain unknown. A model rate does not guarantee every part has a usable time estimate.
Create a fee profile for each sales channel. Enter its percentage fees and fixed fees. Every assembly's pricing estimate shows every fee profile. See Pricing and fees.

Choose an installed slicer and its exact version. This sets the profile catalog shown in selection lists and the default for new file processing. Existing parts keep their saved slicer and version. Estimates use supported file metadata or project presets. There is no separate settings page for farm estimation profiles. Enter connection credentials when you add or edit a printer. For host environment variables, networking, database, and public-origin configuration, see Installation configuration.
The Cost catalog stores prices for materials and services that you use across products. It supports cost estimates. It does not track stock or purchases.

Open Cost catalog → Add cost item. Select the type, category, and unit. Then enter the pricing details. Physical items can be counted or measured. Service rates can apply per product or by time. OpenFarm converts a package price to a price per unit. For example, a roll priced at 40 for 100 m × 100 cm contains 100 m² and costs 0.40/m². A 50 cm × 20 cm cut uses 0.10 m², costing 0.04 before any extra waste allowance. Leave a price blank if it is unknown. Enter zero only when the known price is zero. Quantities and dimensions must be positive. Piece counts must be whole numbers. You cannot change an item's unit if an assembly already uses it.

In the assembly's Cost items section, select an item and enter its use per finished product. Hourly services take minutes per product. For area items, choose direct area or cut dimensions and piece count. Choose what the item Counts as: Production includes the cost in parent assemblies, multiplied by the required quantity. Final packing and delivery includes the cost only when this assembly is the finished product. It excludes that cost from parent assemblies. Packaging and shipping default to final packing and delivery. Check that choice for the actual product.

The assembly's Build panel shows category subtotals, product cost, shipping allowance, and the total including shipping. Missing inputs leave costs partial or unavailable. Area calculations assume you can reuse offcuts. OpenFarm does not calculate an optimized cutting layout. For a standalone part with labor or packaging, use a one-part assembly. Continue with Pricing and fees.
An assembly's Pricing section calculates the expected result of a sale for every configured fee profile. It does not record actual orders, payments, or revenue.

Enter prices for each material and color, and known spool purchase prices. Configure model costs and average power in Settings → Printer costs. Set currency, electricity rate, and optional failure allowance in Settings → General. Add product-specific cost items to the assembly. Printer depreciation and electricity appear as separate Build lines when the model settings, rates, and print-time estimate are available. Missing estimates or rates leave the cost partial or unavailable. The failure allowance applies to filament, depreciation, and electricity. It does not increase packaging, labor, other cost items, or shipping.

Open Settings → Fees and add a profile for each sales channel. Each fee is a % of sale price or Fixed per order amount. Combined percent fees must stay below 100%. To include a monthly fee, calculate a fixed amount per order. For example, 48 per month divided by 400 orders = 0.12 per order. The fee preview excludes production costs. Assembly estimates currently apply each fixed fee once per unit, as if each order contains one unit.

Price keeps the sale amount fixed as costs change. Margin targets profit after fees as a share of the price. Price can differ by fee profile. Markup adds a percentage to cost before fees. Price is the same across fee profiles. A blank rule shows break-even prices. The table shows fees, profit, margin, markup, and maximum discount before loss. An impossible margin target shows no calculated price with an explanation. Costs and fees use the current estimates. A partial cost can overstate expected profit. Complete the missing inputs before you use the estimate for a quote.
OpenFarm's REST API uses paths under /api/v1 on your installation. Use a personal access token for scripts and integrations. Manage tokens from a browser where you are signed in.

Open My profile → Access tokens → Add token. Enter a unique name and an expiry date. Select at least one permission. Clear the date only if you need a token that does not expire. For the printer-list example below, grant printers:list. Create the token. Copy the token credential. OpenFarm shows it only once. Expiry is the end of the selected date in UTC. The default is six months. A user can hold up to 50 unrevoked tokens, including expired ones.

Set OPENFARM_TOKEN securely in your shell or secret manager, then send it in a header over HTTPS: curl --fail-with-body \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $OPENFARM_TOKEN" \ https://farm.example.com/api/v1/printers Do not put credentials in URLs, logs, or source files. Each request requires permission from both the token and its owner's account. If the owner loses a permission, existing tokens also lose that access.

Regenerate immediately replaces the credential and keeps its permissions and expiry date. Update the integration with the new credential. If a token has expired, create a new token. Revoke and Revoke all take effect on subsequent requests. Administrators can revoke another user's tokens. They cannot create or regenerate credentials for that user. The same token also works with the MCP server at /mcp, for AI assistants: see AI assistants. Password changes and resets revoke personal tokens. Disabling the owner's account revokes tokens and sessions. Personal tokens cannot manage accounts, browser sessions, or other tokens. They also cannot connect to SignalR live events. These operations require a browser session.

Use the repository's OpenAPI document for exact routes, request fields, responses, and operation permissions. Generate a contract from a checkout with: cd api/src/OpenFarm.Api dotnet run -- export-openapi Export mode does not initialize the database or start printer workers. The web client is generated from this contract; see Local development.

401: invalid, expired, or revoked credential or browser session. 403: authenticated but missing the endpoint's required permission. 400 / 422: read the validation error or problem response and correct the request. 409: inspect current state before retrying a conflicting operation. When submitting production demand, reuse a submission ID only for the same request. A queued job can start a physical print. Check the current configuration and review the preview before submitting work.

The repository contains these directories: api/: the ASP.NET Core backend. web/: the React application, built with Vite. docs/: this Docusaurus site. dev-notes/: engineering notes. You can build the docs site independently of the farm application.

Install the .NET SDK version specified in api/global.json, Bun, Bash, and PostgreSQL. Follow the root README to configure the database or start its Compose service. From the repository root: dotnet restore api/OpenFarm.slnx ./dev.sh setup ./dev.sh up setup installs web dependencies and slicer bundles, then imports their profiles. API startup and profile import apply database migrations and create initial records automatically. dev.sh does not load .env files. If your database uses different connection settings, set ConnectionStrings__Default in the shell. The web app is at http://localhost:5173, with the HTTP API at http://localhost:6868. Development seed defaults are admin / admin-openfarm unless configured before account creation. Development reset destroys data ./dev.sh reset immediately drops the configured database's public schema and deletes local application data, keys, slicers, and web dependencies. Do not use it to troubleshoot a farm you need to preserve.

From the repository root: ./dev.sh docs Use Node.js 20 or later and Bun. The command installs the frozen docs dependencies and starts Docusaurus at http://localhost:3000 with live reload. Additional options pass through, for example ./dev.sh docs --port 3001 --no-open. Production verification from docs/: cd docs bun run typecheck bun run build bun run serve Local search is generated during the production build. Use the served build to test search; the development server alone does not create its index.

Edit user guides in docs/content/ and their order in docs/sidebars.ts. Describe the current interface and API behavior. Engineering designs, protocol details, and future plans belong in dev-notes/. Application checks remain separate: run bun run test, bun run lint, and bun run build from web/, and the relevant .NET checks for backend changes. Do not hand-edit generated API clients.
The filament catalog describes what material you stock. Physical rolls are separate spool records.

Open Filament → Add filament. Set the vendor, name, material type, and any known price per kilogram. Add the color variants you actually use. Optional low-stock and days-left thresholds help identify replenishment needs. Leave prices blank if they are unknown. Enter zero only when the known cost is zero. A color can override the material's default price.

Assign a filament profile for each printer brand, model, and nozzle size you use. Printers with the same hardware share an assignment row. A color can override the default assignment. If you clear the color override, the color uses the filament's default assignment again. Assignments must match the material, hardware, nozzle, and selected slicer catalog. Inventory can be saved without them, but production requires compatible assignments, including for pre-sliced files. The farm's default slicer determines which catalog appears in profile selection lists. Existing parts keep their saved slicer and exact version, called the slicer pin. If a job needs slicing, the selected profiles must have compatible matches in that slicer's catalog. Already-sliced jobs still need compatible assignments, but OpenFarm does not apply their settings to the toolpaths. See When profiles apply and Profiles and slicers.

Select Production filament for the part's material requirement. OpenFarm then matches the job to a loaded, tracked spool of that catalog color variant. The material and color detected in the file remain visible as source metadata. You can choose another color of the same material. OpenFarm rejects a different known material type. A loaded spool of the exact selected variant satisfies the identity check. Review matching diagnostics for profile constraints or missing assignments.
documents.s: Choose production filament on a part

documents.t: Open a filament to switch between Colors, Spools, Usage, and History. Its color rows summarize stock and consumption. Stock numbers describe registered inventory, so keep spool loading, weights, and corrections current.
Feed units describe the printer's physical material paths. Each has slots where tracked spools can be loaded. Open the printer's feed-unit card to inspect and manage them.

Bambu printers expose AMS positions and external spool paths according to their hardware. The U1 exposes one four-slot toolhead unit, T1–T4, with each slot feeding its corresponding head. The spool record and the printer's reported material are separate. Check both when troubleshooting.

Use Add reloader to describe an external reloader's spool positions. Choose its physical feeding slot and whether it replaces an existing external spool port. The add flow defaults to two slots and an available external port. If replacing a port with a registered spool, transfer it to the selected reloader slot or return it to storage. Occupied destinations are refused. Only one active reloader may replace the same port.

The feeding slot is the spool position actually supplying the printer. Change it when the physical path changes. A selection can exist even when the filament has not been registered, but that does not satisfy production's tracked-spool requirement. Only the selected reloader slot supplies material for job matching. Compatible standby spools can count toward the stock available to continue the print. Port detection reports the replaced printer port. It does not report a separate sensor for each standby slot. If recorded usage finishes a spool, OpenFarm can select another loaded spool in the same reloader as estimated continuation. Check the physical reloader. The record does not confirm that the hardware switched spools successfully.

Removing a reloader returns its tracked spools to storage and keeps their weights and history. OpenFarm archives the reloader, and the original external port becomes available again. Adding it again creates a new unit.
One spool record represents one physical roll. Its states are In storage → Using → Finished. OpenFarm keeps its usage history through these changes.

Use Add spools from the filament workflow. Enter one line per filament/color and roll specification, then set its quantity. Shared purchase details such as supplier, order, and date are entered once for the batch. Set the spool weight, known remaining filament for a partly used roll, and price per spool when known. Full identical rolls can appear grouped on the shelf; expand the group to inspect individual labels.

Physically load the spool into the intended printer feed path. Choose Load spool and select the matching printer, feed unit, and slot. Check that the slot shows the intended inventory record and material. Unload returns the record to storage without discarding its remaining weight. Registration does not physically move filament. A printer's reported material alone does not establish tracked inventory.

OpenFarm links each job's filament to a loaded spool. It estimates consumption from the file sent to the printer. For completed prints, OpenFarm deducts the estimated usage. For stopped prints, it uses available layer or progress information. Object exclusions affect the estimate. Filament use is not simply proportional to the number of good units produced. These are estimates, not scale measurements. Prints started outside OpenFarm can also be tracked when the server can recover their file and spool mapping.

Open a spool for its weight and history. Use Record usage for adjustments such as purging, test extrusion, or drift. Correct the remaining amount when a measured weight is more reliable. If OpenFarm cannot identify a spool or estimate, the print appears under Action required. Open the print and assign a spool or resolve the missing usage information where the controls are available. Make a manual adjustment if necessary. Do not deduct the same usage twice. Use Finish when the roll is exhausted. Feed units and reloaders explains how OpenFarm selects continuation spools.
The production image includes default settings. To change them, enter overrides in .env next to your Compose file. ASP.NET setting names use double underscores, such as Seed__AdminPassword.

Setting Purpose POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_DB Initialize the bundled PostgreSQL database on its first start. Database__Host Database hostname or address. The supplied host-network configuration uses 127.0.0.1. Database__Port PostgreSQL port, normally 5432. ConnectionStrings__Default Optional full connection string; takes precedence over the Database__* settings. Seed__AdminUsername, Seed__AdminEmail, Seed__AdminPassword First administrator, created only if needed. ORIGIN Optional deployment override for Settings → Server → Public URL. Locks the field while set. MCP_MODE Optional deployment override: Disabled, AccessTokens, or SignIn. Locks MCP mode in settings. MCP_ENABLED Optional deployment override. true enables MCP; false disables all MCP and OAuth access. Unset leaves control in Settings. OAUTH_ENABLED Legacy upgrade setting. An explicit true imports sign-in mode once when installation settings are first created. Requires HTTPS ORIGIN. OAuth__RegisterPermitLimit, OAuth__PermitLimit Sign-in requests allowed per minute from one address: app registrations (default 10) and other sign-in requests (default 60). Jwt__SigningKey Optional token signing key. If omitted, OpenFarm generates one and saves it under /data/keys. DataProtection__CertificatePath, DataProtection__CertificatePassword Optional PKCS#12 certificate protecting stored printer-credential encryption keys at rest. PUID, PGID, TZ Data ownership and log time zone. Slicing__MaxConcurrentSlicingOperations Maximum number of slicing operations that can run at the same time. Default: 2. Use deploy/.env.example for the current supported examples. Farm currency and prices are configured in the application under Settings.

Set the Public URL under Settings → Server. For a deployment-controlled HTTPS hostname or Cloudflare Tunnel, you can instead set: ORIGIN=https://farm.example.com Route the entire hostname, including /api and /hubs, to http://<server-ip>:6868. The proxy must allow WebSocket connections for live updates. No separate frontend build or API hostname is needed. ORIGIN must contain a scheme and hostname, with an optional port. Do not include a path other than /, a query, a fragment, or credentials. An invalid value stops startup. Apply changed environment settings by recreating the application: docker compose up -d --force-recreate openfarm With an HTTPS origin, refresh cookies use the Secure attribute, even if the proxy connects to OpenFarm over HTTP. Sign in through that HTTPS hostname. Those cookies do not work for direct HTTP sign-in over the LAN. For trusted local HTTP hosting, leave the saved public URL blank and omit ORIGIN. Removing an override does not clear the saved URL.

MCP is disabled by default. Administrators can enable Access tokens only or Sign-in and access tokens under Settings → AI assistants. The second mode requires an HTTPS public URL, except for localhost development. Changes in Settings apply without restarting. For automated deployments, use: ORIGIN=https://farm.example.com MCP_MODE=SignIn ORIGIN overrides the saved public URL. MCP_MODE overrides the saved mode. MCP_ENABLED=true enables access tokens when the saved mode is disabled; otherwise it keeps the enabled mode. Use MCP_MODE=SignIn to select OAuth. MCP_ENABLED=false disables every mode. An explicit availability or mode override makes the MCP control read-only. Leave both unset to manage MCP in Settings. Do not combine MCP_ENABLED=true with MCP_MODE=Disabled. Environment changes require recreating the application. Changing deployment policy invalidates existing signed-in apps and pending connections on startup. Keep the deployment settings consistent when replacing the application instance. The public URL supplies sign-in addresses and token identity. OpenFarm does not derive them from request hosts or forwarded headers. Route /mcp, /oauth/ and /.well-known/ to OpenFarm. Do not place a login wall in front of discovery or /oauth/token. The request limits count the address that connects to OpenFarm. Behind a proxy, assistants can share one count. Adjust OAuth__PermitLimit if necessary.

When the new installation settings are first created, an explicit OAUTH_ENABLED=true and valid ORIGIN preserve sign-in and existing app grants. This import runs once. Later UI changes are not overwritten by the legacy flag. Remove OAUTH_ENABLED after upgrading; use MCP_MODE for continued deployment control. Installations that previously used token-only MCP must enable MCP after upgrading. Personal access tokens retain their REST access. Changing the public URL or MCP mode in settings invalidates app grants and pending authorizations; users must reconnect their signed-in assistants. Setup steps: AI assistants.

Preserve /data/keys with the database and part files. Losing Data Protection keys makes saved printer credentials unreadable. Replacing the signing key invalidates existing login tokens. See Upgrades and backups before moving an installation.
Use the repository's production Compose files to run OpenFarm and PostgreSQL on a Linux host. The supplied configuration uses host networking so OpenFarm can discover printers on the LAN.

Docker Engine and the Compose plugin. A host that can reach your printers' LAN addresses. Persistent storage for the database and application data. Port 6868 available for the web application and 5432 for PostgreSQL with the supplied host-network layout. The released image is built for linux/amd64. Do not assume an ARM image is available.

Create a directory for the installation. Download these two repository files into it: deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml, saved as docker-compose.yml. deploy/.env.example, saved as .env. If you already have the repository checked out: mkdir -p openfarm-install cp deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml openfarm-install/docker-compose.yml cp deploy/.env.example openfarm-install/.env cd openfarm-install Edit .env before the first start: POSTGRES_USER=openfarm POSTGRES_PASSWORD=replace-with-a-strong-database-password POSTGRES_DB=openfarm Database__Host=127.0.0.1 Seed__AdminUsername=admin Seed__AdminPassword=replace-with-a-strong-admin-password Make sure the configured password matches the database password. PostgreSQL uses initialization variables only when it creates a new volume. The current source Compose file puts OpenFarm on the host network but leaves PostgreSQL on a private container network. Add this inside its existing postgres service so Database__Host=127.0.0.1 can reach it: ports: - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432" Keep the loopback address so the database port is not published to the LAN. If PostgreSQL already runs on the host, configure that database instead of starting a second server on the same port.

docker compose up -d docker compose logs --tail=100 openfarm On startup, OpenFarm applies database migrations, creates the first administrator account, and imports the bundled slicer profiles. Open http://<server-ip>:6868 and sign in with the configured administrator credentials. If you omitted Seed__AdminPassword, the initial password is admin-openfarm. Change it before allowing other people to reach the installation. Seed settings do not reset an existing account's password.

The supplied Compose file uses named volumes data and postgres. Application data is mounted at /data and includes part files and cryptographic keys. Keep both volumes when recreating containers. Host networking supports Bambu SSDP and Snapmaker mDNS discovery. The host's firewall controls which network connections can reach OpenFarm. Restrict database access to the OpenFarm host. If multicast discovery is unavailable with your container network setup, add printers by IP address. One application instance Run exactly one OpenFarm application instance per installation. Do not scale the service or run overlapping application containers against the same database during an upgrade. Continue with Configuration, then the Quick start.
Back up PostgreSQL and the application data volume as one recovery set. A database alone does not contain the uploaded files or keys needed to use stored printer credentials.

For the supplied production Compose file, run these commands from its directory. Let active prints finish first when possible. Pause new work before you stop the application. Stopping OpenFarm keeps files and database records consistent during the backup. backup_dir="backups/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)" mkdir -p "$backup_dir" docker compose stop openfarm docker compose exec -T postgres sh -c 'pg_dump -U "$POSTGRES_USER" "${POSTGRES_DB:-$POSTGRES_USER}"' > "$backup_dir/openfarm.sql" Confirm the dump succeeded before continuing. Copy the stopped application's /data out of its container, which remains available after stopping: docker compose cp openfarm:/data "$backup_dir/application-data" docker compose start openfarm Store the SQL dump, copied data (including keys/), Compose file, .env, and encryption certificates together in a secure location. If a backup step fails, keep previous backups. Restart the application when appropriate. Test recovery on a separate, isolated installation before you rely on the backup.

The MCP settings update adds installation settings to the database. Token-only MCP installations must enable Access tokens only under Settings → AI assistants after upgrading. Existing REST tokens remain valid. An explicit legacy OAUTH_ENABLED=true with a valid ORIGIN preserves sign-in on the first upgrade. See AI assistant configuration. After taking a backup: docker compose pull docker compose stop openfarm docker compose up -d openfarm docker compose logs --tail=100 openfarm Migrations run on startup. Keep the existing project directory and project name so Compose reuses the same named volumes. To control when you upgrade, use a specific release image tag instead of latest. Only one application instance can use the database. Expect brief downtime. Do not run overlapping instances during an upgrade.

Prepare an isolated installation with the application version that matches the backup. Keep OpenFarm stopped and start PostgreSQL only. Restore the dump into an empty database using its configured owner. Restore the contents of the saved application data to the volume mounted at /data. Restore the matching configuration and certificates. Check file ownership against PUID and PGID. Verify that the original encryption keys are present. Start one OpenFarm application instance. Inspect the logs. Confirm sign-in, files, printer credentials, and queued work before returning the farm to use. Rollback requires a compatible application and database schema. Starting an old image against a migrated database is not a restore strategy. Do not use docker compose down -v on an installation whose data you need to keep.
An assembly is a reusable product definition. It contains at least one part or sub-assembly with quantities. Creating one does not create print jobs.

Open Assemblies → Add assembly. Set the name and description. In Structure, use Add part or assembly and set quantities per finished assembly. Add additional Cost items such as hardware, packaging, labor, or shipping as needed. Save the assembly. For nested assemblies, OpenFarm multiplies component quantities through each level. It prevents circular definitions, such as an assembly containing itself. The library selection list can find items across folders. Moving a record to another folder does not change its bill of materials (BOM) references.

For complete products, create a run and request the assembly in sets. OpenFarm expands the whole batch and totals each printed part before splitting it into plate jobs. It does not multiply the rounded plate count for one set by the number of sets. The assembly's direct Print action lets you enter whole-plate counts for each printed component. Use a run's set quantity when you need an exact number of complete products. Non-printed cost items contribute estimated costs, not printer output or stock reservations. A run does not purchase or consume cost-catalog inventory.

The assembly page's Build estimate combines printed materials, configured printer costs, additional costs, and applicable allowances. The Pricing section calculates sale-price estimates against fee profiles. See Costs and pricing. To include packaging or labor for a standalone part, create an assembly containing that part. If inputs are missing, the cost estimate remains partial or unknown.
Parts hold the files and requirements used to create jobs. Start from Parts → Add part.

You can upload STL, 3MF (including sliced .gcode.3mf), and raw .gcode / .gco / .g files. The complete upload request has a 500 MiB limit. Leave space for the form data sent with the file. A supported file extension does not guarantee readable metadata or compatibility with every printer. Use a file prepared for the intended printer; raw G-code cannot safely become a different machine's toolpath just by changing a profile. See When profiles apply for the file decision tree and the separate rules for library estimates, production slicing, and already-sliced jobs.

Upload or drop a file. Set its name and tags. Wait for background processing to finish. Review the extracted plates, material requirements, nozzle, quantity, and estimates. For a multi-plate file, select the plates to save. Complete missing requirements. Choose Production filament for each material line. Confirm the review to save the part records. For sliced 3MF and G-code, OpenFarm reads estimates stored in the file. For unsliced project 3MF, it can calculate estimates from embedded settings or supported named presets. You can review and save STL and geometry-only 3MF without estimates. Unknown time or filament weight stays unknown. It does not become zero.

An Incomplete part can be kept in the library while you fill gaps. Ready to print indicates complete part requirements, while actual dispatch still depends on printer matching. If OpenFarm recognizes the object quantity, you cannot edit it. For files with unknown quantities, you can enter a whole-plate quantity manually. That value does not enable object skipping. Exact quantities require verified object identifiers in the file. See Outcomes and recovery.

Edit the saved details and save your changes. File replacement and reprocessing each have a separate review step. They keep the part's saved slicer and exact version unless you select another slicer. Changing the farm default does not update existing parts. Finite queued jobs retain their captured production inputs. Changing a part does not rewrite running jobs or recorded material consumption.

Use folders, tags, search, and the Details / Thumbnails switch. Move items with Move to or drag them to a supported destination. Folders organize records; they do not set a manual item order. You can remove only empty folders. Moving a part does not change the assemblies that use it.

Profiles generate new toolpaths only when the file needs slicing. STL and unsliced 3MF need slicing. Supported sliced 3MF and raw G-code already contain toolpaths. Changing an OpenFarm profile does not regenerate those toolpaths. There are two separate stages: Library processing reads the uploaded file and, when supported, calculates estimates. It does not select settings from your connected printers or loaded spools. Production file preparation checks the destination printer and its loaded spools. If slicing is needed, OpenFarm uses that printer's configuration and the part's saved slicer engine and exact version. The saved engine and version are called the slicer pin. Pinning a job to a printer is a separate choice. A successful estimate or Ready to print part does not guarantee that a particular printer can take the job. Printer matching still applies.

Profile Where you configure it for production Role when slicing Printer / machine Edit the destination printer → machine profile Supplies machine settings, including machine G-code and nozzle configuration. OpenFarm also checks the registered hardware and the connected printer's nozzle report. Process Edit the destination printer → process profile Supplies the process preset, such as layer height, walls, infill, and support defaults. Filament Edit the filament → assign a profile for the printer brand, model, and nozzle size. A color can override this assignment. Supplies material settings for the tracked spool selected for each required material and color. A printer record describes physical hardware. A machine profile contains slicer settings. A spool record tracks a physical roll of filament. A filament profile contains material settings for the slicer. Selecting a profile does not change the physical nozzle, plate, or material.

The .3mf extension alone does not answer this question. A 3MF archive can contain geometry, project settings, or sliced toolpaths. A project can also retain geometry and settings after slicing. File contents OpenFarm's route STL Unsliced geometry; needs production slicing. Geometry-only 3MF (sometimes called plain 3MF) No supported plate G-code and no recognized embedded project settings; needs production slicing. Unsliced project 3MF No supported plate G-code, but contains project settings; needs production slicing even if OpenFarm successfully estimates it. Sliced 3MF, often named .gcode.3mf Contains a supported Metadata/plate_*.gcode entry. OpenFarm treats the upload as already sliced, even if it also contains project settings and models. Raw .gcode, .gco, or .g Already sliced. OpenFarm looks inside the 3MF archive for supported plate G-code. The .gcode.3mf filename alone does not select the file's processing route. Other vendors' 3MF layouts are not automatically supported. OpenFarm can reject malformed or unsupported files. Unreadable or conflicting metadata can leave requirements or estimates unknown. If an archive contains supported plate G-code, OpenFarm processes the upload as already sliced. This also applies to archives that mix sliced and unsliced plates. OpenFarm does not automatically slice the remaining plates. A requested plate must have usable sliced output. For background on the format, Prusa's Saving projects as 3MF explains why a project can carry settings and modifiers as well as geometry. OpenFarm's own supported entries determine its behavior.
documents.s: Which kind of file did I upload?

documents.t: Library estimates do not use the fleet's selected machine and process profiles or the inventory's filament-profile assignments. There is no separate farm estimation profile to configure. Uploaded file Source of library time and weight estimates Are production profiles applied? STL or geometry-only 3MF No automatic slicing estimate. Complete missing requirements during review; estimates remain unavailable. No. Supported unsliced project 3MF OpenFarm first runs the selected slicer with the project's embedded settings. See the restricted retry below. No; the destination printer and loaded spools are not selected here. Sliced 3MF or raw G-code Metadata already present in the file. OpenFarm does not run the slicer to recalculate it. No. Missing time or weight stays unknown. It does not become zero. If an estimate fails, you can still save a part after reviewing its requirements. Production still needs complete requirements.

OpenFarm can estimate recognized OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio projects from their embedded settings. The settings must be usable, and the selected slicer engine and version must be available. This estimation mode excludes Bambu Studio 2.7.1 on macOS. It does not support Prusa or Cura project settings. The first attempt loads the project without external machine, process, or filament preset files. A second attempt is available only for specific validation, version, or modified-machine errors. For this second attempt, OpenFarm: Reads the machine, process, and filament preset names and the build plate stored in the project. Looks up each preset by name in the selected engine's exact version catalog. Each name must have exactly one match. Checks that the build plate is recognized and the matched presets are compatible. Retries with those catalog presets. This retry replaces the project's global preset settings. It does not reproduce custom edits to those presets. Project geometry and local settings remain inputs to the slicer. The retry requires one distinct nonblank filament preset name. Several slots can share that name. A project with several different filament presets can succeed on the first attempt. It cannot use this retry. Missing presets, multiple matches, or another slicing failure leave the estimate unavailable. This retry does not select your fleet's production profiles. Production dispatch does not use this retry as a fallback.
documents.s: Project settings and the named-preset retry

documents.t: For an unsliced upload, the toolpath generated for estimation is temporary. OpenFarm saves the estimates and thumbnails, then discards that toolpath. It slices the stored source again when preparing a production job.
documents.s: Estimating does not make the source file pre-sliced

documents.t: Direct part printing, assembly printing, runs with fixed quantities, and continuous backfill all create queue work. They use the same file preparation and dispatch checks. Pinning a job restricts it to one printer. It does not bypass those checks.
documents.s: When a job is prepared for a printer

documents.t: For each destination printer, OpenFarm: Checks that the job's requirements are complete and current printer reports confirm the nozzle size. Checks the machine profile and finds matching tracked spools on active feed paths. Selects each spool's filament-profile assignment for that printer hardware and nozzle size. A color override takes priority over the filament default. Requires the printer's machine profile, process profile, and build plate, plus the job's exact slicer engine and version pin. Finds compatible presets and their inherited settings in the pinned catalog. Checks each required filament separately, including its bed-temperature setting for the selected plate. Supplies those presets to the slicer and slices the part's selected project plate. Rechecks the current configuration and stock before sending. If a check or slicing fails, OpenFarm sends nothing. A profile constraint saved on a part or job must agree with the loaded spool's assignment. It cannot select a replacement preset. Spools in storage or on another printer are not fallbacks. Setting source Used to generate the production file? Destination printer's machine profile Yes, after resolution and validation. Destination printer's process profile Yes, after resolution and validation. Destination printer's selected build plate Yes. OpenFarm adds the plate selection to the process settings. Filament-profile assignments for the selected tracked spools Yes, after matching and compatibility checks, for each required filament slot. Project's global machine, process, and filament preset settings OpenFarm loads the selected external presets with priority over these project settings. Project geometry, placement, painting, modifiers, and object or part settings OpenFarm still passes these to the slicer. Local overrides can affect the result. The OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio command-line interfaces (CLIs) give external presets priority over project-level settings. They do not erase every local override. Selecting a process preset does not necessarily remove an object's custom infill or support settings. See the loading priority in the OrcaSlicer 2.3.1 CLI implementation and Bambu Studio 2.7.1 CLI implementation. For multi-color projects, OpenFarm matches each project slot to a job line by its detected material and color. It loads the matched filament profile for each slot, in slot order. A slot known to be unused on that plate needs no separate job line. If a used slot has no match, OpenFarm blocks the job. It does not keep an embedded filament preset as a substitute. STL and geometry-only files without project slots cannot supply several independent filament lines this way. Production profile matching supports OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio. A SuperSlicer CLI adapter exists in the code, but it does not support these profile catalogs. It cannot bypass a missing or incompatible profile.
documents.s: STL and unsliced 3MF: generate a new production file

documents.t: OpenFarm does not re-slice these files or apply the destination printer's profiles to their toolpaths. Configuration What happens for an already-sliced job? Machine profile Required and validated against registered hardware and the current nozzle report when OpenFarm selects loaded filament. OpenFarm does not apply its settings to the toolpaths. Process profile Not required for this route and not applied to the toolpaths. Filament-profile assignments Required and validated for the loaded, tracked spools. OpenFarm checks material, nozzle, machine, and saved profile constraints. It does not replace toolpath settings such as temperature, flow, or cooling. Build plate OpenFarm does not select a new slicing plate or validate its profile temperature for this route. Prepare the file for the physical plate you will use. Part's slicer pin No slicer is run. OpenFarm does not look up these validation assignments in a pinned slicer catalog. For real supported printers, the file must declare a recognizable target printer model matching the destination. A missing target, an unrecognized target, or a different model blocks the job. This model check does not apply to the simulator. Entering a missing nozzle or material requirement manually does not add a missing printer-model declaration to the sliced file. Temperatures, speeds, layer height, supports, and other toolpath choices remain those of the original slice. Choosing another spool color changes which physical stock can match the job. It does not rewrite the file's slicing settings. Existing toolpaths can still need execution preparation OpenFarm can still prepare the file for a partial plate or supported object skipping. It can also package or adapt the file for the printer's protocol. The uploaded bytes can therefore differ from the stored file. These operations do not apply slicing profiles. See Outcomes and recovery.
documents.s: Sliced 3MF and raw G-code: keep the existing toolpaths

documents.t: Downloading a part's original file returns the stored upload without applying profiles. It does not export the temporary library-estimation result. A job file download returns the file saved for that job, if available. Otherwise, OpenFarm prepares a production file as described above. This requires an assigned or pinned target printer. Downloading a saved job file does not slice it again with today's profiles. OpenFarm can observe a print started outside its queue. This is a printer-started print. Observing it does not cause OpenFarm to slice it or apply profile settings.
documents.s: Original downloads, job downloads, and printer-started prints

documents.t: This section applies when OpenFarm slices a production file. A selected profile can come from a different catalog than the part's pinned slicer: Saved choice Resolution for production slicing System preset already in the pinned engine and version Use that preset. System preset from another version of the same engine Find a match by vendor and external preset ID. A renamed preset can match. Without an ID, use vendor and name. System preset from the other supported engine Require an exact match by external ID, vendor, and name. A similar display name is insufficient. User preset made for the pinned engine Use the user preset. Match its inherited system presets to the pinned catalog. User preset from another engine Block. OpenFarm blocks slicing if a preset is missing, has multiple matches, or is incompatible. It also blocks missing catalogs, unavailable slicers, and inherited presets or templates that it cannot load. It does not substitute a similar preset, another engine, or a newer version.
documents.s: Which version of a profile is used?

documents.t: Change Effect Change the farm default slicer Changes the default for new processing and the catalog shown in profile lists. Existing parts and jobs keep their pins. Replace or reprocess an unsliced part Keeps its current pin unless you choose another slicer. A part without a pin can use the farm default. Reads requirements and estimates again using the applicable route above. Reprocess a sliced file Reads its metadata again. Does not regenerate toolpaths with your current profiles. Change printer machine, process, or plate settings, or a filament assignment OpenFarm uses or checks the new configuration on the next production preparation, according to the file route. Saved library estimates stay unchanged. Change settings or loaded spools while a file is being generated Dispatch checks fresh state again. A configuration mismatch stops the send and leaves the job for retry. Edit a library part after jobs with fixed quantities were queued Those jobs keep their saved source inputs and pin. OpenFarm still checks current printer settings and spool assignments. Continuous backfill can use the updated part before dispatch. To keep an external slicer's toolpaths, upload its supported sliced output. To generate toolpaths with your destination printer's profiles, upload STL or a supported unsliced 3MF. Either route still needs compatible hardware, material, and configuration. Use Job diagnosis to see why a printer cannot take a job. After production slicing, the job records the slicer and profiles used for that slice. The library estimate can use different settings.
documents.s: What happens after I change something?

documents.t: Profiles are saved slicer settings, also called presets. They are separate from physical printer and spool records. The Profiles page has separate catalogs for machine, process, and filament profiles. See When profiles apply for the rules for STL, geometry-only 3MF, project 3MF, sliced 3MF, and G-code.

The production image includes the slicers listed in the repository manifest. On startup, OpenFarm imports their system profiles. Each slicer engine and version has its own catalog. Choose the farm's default slicer engine and exact version under Settings → Slicing defaults. This determines the catalog shown in selection lists and the default for new file processing. Existing parts keep their saved engine and version, called the slicer pin.

Open Profiles → Import profiles. The UI accepts .zip, .orca_printer, .orca_filament, .bbscfg, and .bbsflmt bundles, with a 20 MiB request body limit. Upload the bundle. Review the machine and filament presets found in it. Select the presets to import. Confirm the import. OpenFarm saves nothing before confirmation. A preset embedded in a project is not necessarily available as an import.

The printer selects machine and process profiles and its build plate. The filament assigns a profile for each printer model and nozzle size. A color can override that assignment. The part keeps its saved slicer engine and exact version for file processing and production slicing. Unsliced multi-color projects need compatible profiles for every required material slot. Pre-sliced files keep their toolpaths and must match the model they declare.

If a job needs slicing, OpenFarm finds the selected presets in the part's pinned slicer catalog. A matching system preset can come from another supported catalog. A user preset from another slicer engine is blocked. Missing profiles, multiple matches, unloaded catalogs, and incompatible presets stop the job. OpenFarm does not substitute another preset. Already-sliced files skip this catalog matching. They still require a compatible machine profile and filament-profile assignments for loaded spools. Open Job diagnosis to see the requirement and a link to the relevant settings. If profiles are missing after a local setup, run the profile-import step in Local development. Find the cause of a compatibility failure before changing the slicer pin.
The Dashboard shows camera tiles, current prints, and printer warnings. Use it to find machines that need attention. Open the printer or job page to use its controls.

Each browser tab uses one live connection for printer and job updates. OpenFarm refreshes camera images while they are visible. The images are periodic snapshots, not video recordings. If a camera image stops updating, check the camera connection separately from MQTT or Moonraker status. If all live updates stop, check the browser connection and the reverse proxy's WebSocket support for /hubs/farm.

Inspect and remove the printed output before you mark the printer ready. A finished tile means you must inspect and clear the bed. It does not confirm that every unit is acceptable. See Outcomes and recovery for output confirmation and replacements.

Users with audit access can open Activity log under Administration. The log shows recorded changes and who made them. Use it to investigate configuration updates, printer events, job actions, and skipped material deductions. The activity log is not the source for utilization hours. Stats uses dedicated printer-activity history and print records, including gaps when the server could not observe a machine.
Create a maintenance task once and assign it to printers. Each assigned printer has its own service cycle.

Open Maintenance → Add task. Give the task a name and at least one positive interval: days, print hours, or print count. Choose a warning threshold and the printers to enroll. Save the task. Existing templates can also be added from a printer's maintenance card using Add tasks. Seeded tasks are editable templates. Choose intervals based on the printer and operating conditions. Editing a shared task changes the definition for every enrolled printer.

If a task has several intervals, it becomes due when the first interval is reached. The default warning threshold is 80%. Due soon warns before an interval is reached. Overdue means at least one interval has been reached. Hours use recorded printer activity and print durations. A ≥ indicator means actual hours can be higher because OpenFarm could not track some time. Failed prints, cancelled prints, and observed printer-started prints can also contribute to wear. Overdue maintenance currently warns only; it does not block automatic dispatch. Pause or otherwise manage work before physically servicing a printer.

After you complete the service, choose Mark done. Add a note if necessary. A service date cannot be in the future or before the current cycle began. OpenFarm records the signed-in user as the person who did the service. Use Set last done to record service completed before OpenFarm began tracking it. Include known usage since that service. OpenFarm keeps the history if you later remove the task or printer. The page has views for tasks needing attention, all tasks, task definitions, and history. Recording completed service requires different permissions from managing or removing task definitions.
Open Stats to review the farm over a selected date range and compare it with the preceding equivalent period.

Figure Interpretation Prints and success Includes ended prints that actually started. Success rate is completed prints divided by all completed, failed, and cancelled attempts. Printer time Recorded periods of printing, awaiting-clear, paused, idle, and offline status. Unobserved time appears as no data. Utilization Printing hours divided by observed hours. Offline time is observed; unknown time is excluded. Queue wait Time from job creation to start, summarized for jobs that started in the range. Filament and waste Compares recorded or estimated material use for completed work with material use for failed and cancelled work. Units made Stats uses the recorded plate quantities of completed jobs. Use job and run outcome details to verify the exact accepted output.

The date range uses local days in the browser's time zone. The API accepts an IANA time zone and supports up to 366 days. OpenFarm groups prints by their end date, not their queue date. Time comes from printer activity. Output comes from print records. A print that has not ended does not contribute a completed duration. Server downtime can leave periods with no data. OpenFarm cannot reconstruct every print that started and ended while the server was offline.

OpenFarm estimates material use from files and observed print progress. Recorded material cost uses the price saved when OpenFarm deducted the usage. Later catalog price changes do not change that recorded cost. Missing prices or deductions can leave the report incomplete. Use the filament's Usage / History, spool history, and Action required print entries to investigate discrepancies. These reports do not measure filament on a scale or record sales revenue.
The normal workflow is: define a part, load a compatible spool, request output, and let a ready printer take the resulting job.

Record What it represents Part A saved source file or selected plate, its print requirements, and production filament choices. Assembly A product definition containing parts and sub-assemblies with quantities. Cost items can be added separately. Filament and color A catalog material identity and its color variants, prices, and profile assignments. Spool A physical roll, with remaining weight, purchase details, and usage history. Feed unit and slot The printer's material path: AMS, external spool, toolheads, or a configured reloader. A tracked spool is loaded into a slot. Profile Slicer settings for a machine, process, or filament. Profiles are separate from physical inventory.

Production demand describes what you want to make. It can exist without a run. A print job is one attempt to print a plate. OpenFarm assigns it automatically, or you pin it to a specific printer. A run groups a fixed production target so you can track an order or batch. Parts can be requested in whole plates or unit targets; assemblies in a run are requested in complete sets. Exact unit targets can require a partial final plate, which needs reliable object identities. Runs explains this planning flow. Continuous backfill repeatedly makes whole plates when compatible printers are idle, after jobs with fixed quantities. You can pause it and limit how many printers it uses at the same time.

A saved part can be incomplete. A complete part can still have no matching printer. A matching printer can be busy or waiting for bed clearance. Production checks connectivity, availability, confirmed nozzle sizes, file compatibility, tracked loaded spools, profiles, and stock where estimates are known. Use Job diagnosis to see which layer is blocking work.

Jobs with fixed quantities save their production inputs when queued. Running jobs keep those saved inputs. Backfill uses current part inputs until OpenFarm prepares and sends the job. OpenFarm still checks current printer settings before sending. Editing a library record does not rewrite a completed print's material history. Requeue uses retained production inputs; Outcomes and recovery covers the limits.

Term Meaning in these guides Toolpath The movement and extrusion instructions generated by a slicer. G-code contains toolpaths. Metadata Information stored with a file, such as its material, nozzle size, or estimated print time. Preset or profile A saved set of slicer settings. OpenFarm groups profiles into catalogs by slicer and version. Slicer pin The slicer engine and exact version saved for a part. It is separate from pinning a job to a printer. Pinned printer The only printer that a job is allowed to use. The job must still pass compatibility checks. Production snapshot The source file reference, requirements, and slicer selection saved for a job. Current printer settings and loaded spools are still checked. Object identity An identifier in the file that lets OpenFarm distinguish a printable object for quantity checks or object skipping. Dispatch The process of preparing a job and sending it to a printer.
OpenFarm manages a 3D print farm from one web application. You run it on your own server, keep the database and files, and connect directly to supported printers on your LAN.

Monitor the fleet, printer status, cameras, and current work. Track filament colors, physical spools, loaded slots, usage, and estimated material costs. Store parts, import slicer profiles, and build nested assemblies. Queue plates directly, plan finite runs, and fill spare capacity with continuous backfill. Diagnose why a printer cannot take a job, then follow the link to its configuration. Track maintenance, production statistics, cost estimates, and product pricing. Give team members specific permissions and issue scoped API tokens.

Each installation serves one farm. Run one application instance with PostgreSQL. That instance manages printer connections and sends jobs to printers. You can use the browser remotely, but the server must have network access to the printers. See Installation for deployment and Supported printers for the actual model catalog.

The application groups daily work under Operate and reusable records under Library. Settings and account administration are separate. Start with the Quick start, then read Key concepts when you need to understand how parts, spools, jobs, and runs relate.
Bambu printers connect directly over the LAN. OpenFarm does not ask for a Bambu Cloud account.

Confirm the model is in the supported catalog. Enable LAN-only access and Developer Mode where required by the printer's firmware. Find its IP address, serial number, and LAN access code in the printer settings. Make sure the OpenFarm server can reach the printer. Enabling LAN-only mode changes how you use the printer with Bambu Cloud and its apps.

Open Printers → Add printer. Select the discovered printer. For manual entry, set the brand, model, IP address, and serial number. Enter a name and the LAN access code. Add the printer. OpenFarm verifies the connection before saving the printer. Credentials stay encrypted on the server. Enter or replace them from the printer's add/edit page.

Wait for the connected printer to report its nozzle size. Edit the printer and select a compatible machine profile, process profile, and build plate. Register the physical spools and assign compatible filament profiles. Then load the tracked spools into the correct AMS or external slots. Pre-sliced files must match the model they were sliced for. Being able to connect does not mean an arbitrary sliced file is compatible.

MQTT status/control: TCP 8883. FTPS file transfer: TCP 990, plus the passive data connections negotiated by the printer. Camera: TCP 322 for the cataloged X1 models; 6000 for P1/A1 models. Discovery: UDP 2021/1990 on the server's LAN. A working status connection does not confirm that file transfer and camera connections also work. If a bridged container cannot discover printers, add the printer by IP address. You can also use the supplied Linux host-network configuration. See Troubleshooting. X1-family cameras use RTSP, which the current application does not relay. Those models can connect for status/production while their camera view remains unavailable. P1/A1 snapshot cameras are supported.
Use Printers for the fleet list and open a printer for its camera, current job, hardware, feed units, maintenance, profiles, and recent activity.

Connection status and print status are separate. If a printer disconnects, OpenFarm still keeps its bed-clearance state. Idle: no active print is reported. Printing / Paused: an active print is running or paused. Awaiting clear: the printer finished or stopped a print and needs operator clearance. Offline: the server cannot currently reach the printer. Check the printer-reported state and alerts as well as OpenFarm's status. Camera images are snapshots refreshed while visible, not a recording archive.
Remove the finished or failed print. Inspect the bed and material path. Choose Mark ready. The printer becomes available for queued work. A compatible job can then start automatically.

Use Edit to change the name, connection settings, profiles, and compatible build plate. Changing connection information triggers verification. Select a machine profile only after current telemetry confirms the relevant nozzle size. Machine and process profiles generate toolpaths only for files that need slicing. Already-sliced jobs still need a compatible machine profile. See When profiles apply before expecting a profile change to alter G-code or sliced 3MF toolpaths. A last-known nozzle value can remain visible while offline; production needs confirmation from the current connection. See Printer matching when the displayed size seems correct but a job is blocked.

Removal requires the corresponding permission and confirmation. Do not remove a printer to pause its queue. Resolve active work first. If you remove a printer with an open tracked print, OpenFarm records that print as failed. Historical print records remain available.
OpenFarm connects to the U1's existing Moonraker API over HTTP and WebSocket on port 7125. No extra agent is installed on the printer.

Put the OpenFarm server on a network that can reach the U1. Open Printers → Add printer. Select the discovered U1. For manual entry, enter its IP address with brand Snapmaker, model U1. Enter a name. If the printer requires an API key, enter it. Add the printer. OpenFarm reads the serial number from the printer and verifies its identity. Discovery uses mDNS on UDP 5353. If discovery finds no printer, you can still connect manually. DHCP can assign a saved IP address to a different U1. If its serial number does not match, OpenFarm keeps the printer offline. Correct the saved IP address.

Use OrcaSlicer for U1 production; Bambu Studio does not provide U1 presets. Choose the compatible machine and process profiles and the supported high-temperature build plate. The U1 appears with four toolhead slots T1–T4. Load tracked spools into their actual slots. Each required filament must be on a head with the nozzle size the part needs.
