Heads can have different nozzle sizes; a preset at one diameter does not make every head compatible. OpenFarm uploads G-code, configures the tool-to-head mapping, and starts the print through Moonraker. A successful connection check does not confirm that every print operation works on your firmware version. The chamber camera requires HTTP access to the printer on port 80. OpenFarm keeps the camera awake while it monitors the printer. If a start request loses its response, OpenFarm waits for printer telemetry instead of sending the start again. Check the printer before you retry an unconfirmed print.

Review the outcome and object-skipping guide before you use partial plates or live exclusions. OpenFarm can count compatible standby stock toward the filament available for a print. Confirm that the U1's physical auto-replenish settings can use that stock.
OpenFarm uses its hardware catalog to select the printer connection software. Only models in this catalog are supported. A similar model is not automatically compatible.

Brand Models Connection Bambu Lab X1, X1 Carbon (X1C), X1E, P1P, P1S, A1, A1 mini (A1MINI) Direct LAN, access code required. Snapmaker U1 Moonraker over LAN; API key when required by the printer. System Simulation Software simulator for development, not physical hardware. This list follows PrinterModelCatalog in the codebase. Newer Bambu models are not implicitly supported. Camera support is separate: P1/A1 snapshot cameras and the U1 HTTP camera are supported. X1-family RTSP relay is not implemented in the current application.

Make the printer reachable from the OpenFarm server, even if you use the web UI from another machine. Reserve its LAN address where possible. Prepare Bambu LAN access or Snapmaker Moonraker access. Match the physical nozzle and build plate to production configuration. If discovery does not find a printer, use manual entry on Add printer. Discovery needs local broadcast or multicast traffic. A direct connection by IP address can still work when discovery is unavailable.
Backfill repeatedly prints whole plates until you pause or remove the entry. It uses compatible printers that are available after jobs with fixed quantities.

Open a part or assembly's Print flow and enable Continuous backfill. Submit the entry, then manage it from Queue. By default, the entry uses one printer at a time. The entry remains visible even when it has no current jobs. You can limit how many printers it uses at once or pin it to one printer. You can also pause, resume, refresh, or remove it.

For assembly backfill, OpenFarm saves the number of each printed part needed for one assembly set. It compares these quantities with completed units and units already allocated to queued or running work. It gives priority to the eligible part furthest behind the proportions needed for the next complete set. If one part cannot print, this balancing limits excess production of the other parts. Failed and cancelled jobs do not count as completed output. Each selected part must still match a ready printer.

Pause blocks new dispatches and retries. It does not physically cancel an already running print. Refresh uses the assembly's current bill of materials (BOM). It replaces old requirements, cancels unsent jobs, and starts a new balancing period. Running prints remain linked to the original assembly recipe. Remove cancels unsent work and retains running prints and history. Backfill uses the current part file until OpenFarm prepares and sends a job. Changing a part file alone does not require an assembly recipe refresh. For an order with a fixed quantity and a defined end, use a run.

Open Job diagnosis on the job page, or select the blocking status in the queue row. The dialog checks current requirements for each printer. It shows the results and links to the settings you need to change.

Check What to verify Availability Printer is reachable, not busy, and has been cleared when required. Assignment A pinned job can use only its selected printer. Queue position and preference are separate from compatibility. Nozzle Reports from the current connection confirm the required diameter on every head and feed path the job uses. Target model Pre-sliced files match their declared target model. Material Required filament is physically loaded and registered as an active tracked spool. Identity The loaded spool matches the selected production color variant or the material and color requirements saved for the job. Profiles All jobs need a compatible machine profile and filament-profile assignments for loaded spools. If a job needs slicing, it also needs a process profile. All three presets must have compatible matches in the job's pinned slicer catalog. Build plate A required slicing plate is selected and compatible. Stock Known estimated use plus the fixed 10% margin fits available compatible stock.

For a 120 g estimate, the initial check requires 132 g, including the 10% margin. Compatible standby spools in the same AMS or configured reloader can contribute stock for continuation. An external spool by itself supplies only its own stock. Standby reloader slots do not count as separate active material choices. Unknown need does not block the stock check. After slicing, OpenFarm checks again using the generated file's exact grams. If it no longer fits, nothing is sent. Load more stock or correct a measured spool weight, then reevaluate.

Use When profiles apply to distinguish settings used to slice a new file from profiles checked for an already-sliced file. Pre-sliced jobs do not apply your current process and filament settings to existing toolpaths. A saved nozzle size from an offline printer is not current confirmation. Reconnect the printer and wait for a fresh nozzle report. Select a compatible machine profile, then check the filament assignments for that hardware and nozzle size. Changing the farm default does not change an existing part's saved slicer and version. If slicing is needed, a profile missing from that slicer's catalog can block the job. A user preset from another slicer can also block it. A similar name in another catalog is not enough.

Last attempt failed reports an error after the job passed compatibility checks, such as slicing or file transfer. Inspect the reason and server logs. Repeated dispatch failures use a growing retry delay. Opening or refreshing diagnosis is read-only and does not itself dispatch the job.
A completed printer command is not always a verified count of good output. Inspect the physical plate before confirming quantities or clearing the bed.

For a fixed target of units or sets, OpenFarm can select a partial final plate if the file has reliable object identifiers. Every recognized printable object instance counts as one unit. Modifiers, supports, and shared purge structures are not extra units. The job's object controls show whether live skipping is available. OpenFarm needs supported object identifiers that match the file used for the active print. A reliable object count alone is not enough. For example, raw Bambu G-code can contain object counts but lack the identifier table needed to skip objects. Prefer a labeled sliced 3MF for that workflow. Object exclusions use native Bambu or U1 commands. Verify firmware behavior on your hardware before depending on partial plates. Purge and shared structures may still print.

Output can remain unverified if object-skip confirmation is missing or the print ended during a connection interruption. Inspect the actual plate before you use Confirm produced units. Until you confirm the output, OpenFarm can block replacement or write-off actions for that completed attempt. Failed and cancelled attempts conservatively record zero produced units. Their material estimates can still count consumed filament.

Requeue missing units creates a replacement for the unresolved shortfall, retaining the original production snapshot. Write off missing units accepts the remaining loss without calling it produced stock. These operations preserve the original attempt and prevent resolving the same loss twice. Existing legacy whole-plate jobs may offer Requeue plate.

If OpenFarm cannot confirm a start request that uses object controls, it does not automatically send the request again. Check the printer first. The print might have started despite the network failure. If the printer is idle and the bed is clear, use Confirm print did not start. This cancels the attempt so you can requeue it.
documents.s: When the start acknowledgement is uncertain

documents.t: For sent jobs, downloads use the saved file prepared for that job. OpenFarm does not slice it again with current settings. For Bambu printers, the start request specifies the initial object exclusions. If you print the downloaded file outside OpenFarm, apply those exclusions again. U1 downloads already include their initial exclusion commands. Filament use remains an estimate that includes purge and extrusion before observed skips. It is not simply proportional to good-unit counts.
The queue holds physical plate attempts. You can print directly from a part or assembly without creating a production run.

Open a part and choose Print. Select the number of whole plates, review the plan, and choose Send to queue. For an assembly's direct Print flow, set whole-plate counts per component; zero skips a component. For an exact unit target or complete assembly sets, use Runs. For repeat production during idle capacity, use Continuous backfill. Ready printers may start A queued job can start automatically on a compatible idle printer. Before you send work to the queue, check the physical bed and material path.

Open Queue and use its status tabs and part-name search. A job page shows the printer, production inputs, matched profiles, outcome, file, and available actions. Each printer shows progress while OpenFarm prepares and uploads its file. Physical printing starts separately. Queue ordering affects selection among eligible jobs. Compatibility is a separate decision: a job near the top may remain blocked while a later compatible job runs.

The row action menu shows the operations available for that job: Move to top changes waiting priority. Pin to printer restricts the job to one printer. Unpin restores automatic assignment. Remove job cancels unsent work after confirmation. Pinning does not bypass matching. A pinned job waits if its printer is busy, offline, missing material, or incompatible. Open the blocking status or Job diagnosis for details.

Pause, resume, and cancel are offered only for eligible jobs and accounts with explicit remote-control permission. Confirm the physical outcome after a stop. Printer-started prints are tracked separately from OpenFarm-dispatched jobs when observable. They can have incomplete file or spool information and do not become queued demand or run progress automatically.
A run groups an order or batch with fixed quantities. Use it to track progress and confirm completion. Direct queue jobs do not require a run.

Open Runs → Add run. Use Add part or assembly under Items to make. For a part, choose whole Plates or a Unit target. For an assembly, enter complete Sets. Choose automatic assignment or a specific printer for each line. Review required units, planned plates, and estimates. Enter the run details. Submit using Add run. The run's jobs appear in Queue. OpenFarm checks the plan again when you submit it. If library inputs changed during planning, refresh the plan and review the updated quantities before submitting again.

Suppose five assembly sets need two brackets each and the part contains six brackets per plate. The total is ten brackets: one job targets six and another targets four. Partial plates require reliable identifiers for complete printable units and a file that supports the required object selection. A quantity estimate alone is insufficient. If OpenFarm cannot verify safe selection, it blocks the operation. See Outcomes and recovery. Parts requested in Plates remain whole-plate jobs. Continuous backfill also schedules whole plates.

Open the run to see its lines, plate states, produced output, and unresolved shortfalls. Failed or cancelled attempts remain separate from their replacements in the history. Inspect output before confirming unknown quantities. Use Requeue missing units to replace an unresolved shortfall. Use Write off missing units to accept the loss. Available close and completion actions depend on the run's progress and unresolved work. Cancelling a run does not erase prints that already happened. Jobs with fixed quantities keep the source inputs saved when queued. OpenFarm still checks current printer settings and loaded spools before sending each job. Creating a plan does not reserve a printer configuration or its stock.
OpenFarm is developed in the getopenfarm/openfarm repository. Use its issue tracker for bugs and feature requests.

Include these details: Application version or image tag. Installation method. Affected printer model and firmware version. Steps to reproduce the problem. Expected result and actual error. For a job problem, include its matching diagnosis. State whether you printed directly, created a run, or used backfill. Provide a small sample file only if you can share it. Before sharing logs or configuration, remove access codes, API tokens, signing keys, passwords, and personal data.

Use Edit this page to propose a documentation change. Guides live in docs/content/; navigation order lives in docs/sidebars.ts. Follow the local docs workflow and build before opening a pull request. Describe the current product behavior and use the UI's actual action names. Keep future ideas and implementation notes in dev-notes/ so operators can follow the guides without mistaking planned work for a shipped feature. Use short, active sentences and consistent technical terms. Explain unfamiliar OpenFarm terms and give each numbered step one main action. Keep commands, interface labels, technical limits, and behavior exceptions accurate.
Open the affected printer or job page and read the error. Change one relevant setting at a time, then check the result.

If ORIGIN uses HTTPS, sign in through that hostname. Direct HTTP LAN access cannot send Secure refresh cookies. Route /api and /hubs through the same hostname. Confirm that the configured origin has no path other than / and no query. An existing account's password is not changed by editing Seed__AdminPassword. Ask another administrator to reset it. See Accounts.

For local development, check that ConnectionStrings__Default includes a password and matches the database user and port. dev.sh does not load Compose .env files. PostgreSQL checks authentication before it runs migrations. Recreating tables does not fix incorrect credentials. For Docker, initialization variables do not change passwords in an existing volume. Check the original credentials and keep the volume's data. If a PostgreSQL service already uses port 5432, resolve the conflict before starting the supplied host-network configuration.

Discovery happens on the server's LAN. The browser's network does not control it. Check Bambu UDP 2021/1990 or U1 mDNS UDP 5353, as applicable. Also check the host and container network settings. Bridged containers might not receive multicast traffic. If a direct connection works, enter the printer's IP address manually.

Check power, the IP address, DHCP reservation, credentials, and model support. Then check the relevant Bambu or U1 ports. Status, file transfer, and camera use separate connections. A U1 serial mismatch can indicate that DHCP reassigned the IP address. X1-family camera views are unavailable because the current app has no RTSP relay; opening the camera port does not enable that feature. If all browser live updates stop together, check WebSockets for /hubs/farm and sign in again if the browser session expired.
documents.s: Printer is offline or a camera is stale

documents.t: Open Job diagnosis and work through Printer matching. Check bed clearance, printer assignment, confirmed nozzle, loaded tracked spool and color, profiles, and plate. Known estimated use must fit the available stock with the 10% margin. A printer-reported material alone is not a registered spool. An offline remembered nozzle is not current confirmation. Pinning does not bypass either check.

Check Settings → Slicing defaults and the installed profile catalogs. Confirm the part's saved slicer and version, then check each filament's assignment for the printer model and nozzle size. For local development, run ./dev.sh slicers and ./dev.sh ingest. U1 production needs an OrcaSlicer selection and compatible U1 presets. Bambu Studio does not provide those presets. If slicing is needed, each selected profile must have a compatible match in the pinned slicer's catalog. A similar name in another catalog is not enough. A user preset from another slicer also blocks slicing.

You can save STL and geometry-only 3MF files without estimates. Missing time or filament weight remains unknown. Review the required material and nozzle fields, then finish the file review. If you correct the source file or quantity, reprocess the part. See Parts.
documents.s: Upload has no estimate or is incomplete

documents.t: The file must contain reliable object identifiers. Raw Bambu G-code can have object counts without the table needed to skip objects. Before using Confirm produced units, inspect the physical plate. If the start result is uncertain, check the printer before using Confirm print did not start. See Recovery.
documents.s: Partial plate or output confirmation is blocked

documents.t: Check Action required entries, the spool assignment, remaining weight, and file estimates. A missing deduction does not mean no filament was used. If necessary, correct the weight from a measurement or record usage manually. Do not deduct the same usage twice. Blank prices leave costs partial.
documents.s: Material use or cost is missing

documents.t: For the supplied deployment: docker compose logs --tail=200 openfarm docker compose logs --tail=100 postgres Record the error, affected job or printer, and time. Remove credentials and sensitive configuration before sharing. Use Support to report a reproducible issue.
